Operate a fleet of remotely managed physical Linux servers and the virtual machines and containers on them: storage, capacity planning and hardware replacement. Own the operating-system lifecycle: patch testing, staged deployment, operating-system and kernel upgrades, tracking exceptions, and moving systems off releases that reach end of life. Keep configurations consistent, and find and correct configuration drift. Networks, cloud and development services Design, run and troubleshoot the network: routing, traffic shaping, firewalls, DHCP and DNS, and the overlay network that connects the data centers, the cloud and remote staff. Manage our resources in AWS, mainly EC2 and S3. Run the self-hosted development services, including GitLab, CI runners, build machines and package mirrors. Monitor the systems, and improve monitoring and alerting so that problems are caught early without needless noise. Lead incident response, contribute to incident reviews, and complete the corrective actions that keep a problem from recurring. Work with developers, IT, data-center staff and hardware vendors when a problem crosses system boundaries. Escalate when needed, with clear findings, the supporting evidence, and a record of the troubleshooting already done. Keep configuration and automation in git, test changes, and make changes through merge requests, review and automated deployment rather than by editing live systems. Security and operational reliability Own access control and security: SSH keys and hardware security keys, network access policies, least privilege, security baselines, timely patching, vulnerability scanning, audits of exposed services, and software supply-chain risk.
